---
title: "Finance and Pay Start migration"
description: "Inventory the Finance canary and Pay integration before adopting the shared Start bridge."
---

Finance and Pay retain their Next.js entrypoints during preparation. Their Start
conversion consumes `@tuturuuu/start-bridge`; neither app owns a copy of its
Next adapters, request context, proxy, server-function transport, or cohort
selector. This page records the conversion requirements, not runtime acceptance.

## Refresh the source inventory

Run these commands from the repository root after a frozen dependency install:

```bash
node apps/finance/migration/inventory.mjs finance > /tmp/finance-inventory.json
node apps/finance/migration/inventory.mjs pay > /tmp/pay-inventory.json
node --test apps/finance/migration/inventory.test.mjs
```

The tool reuses the repository's Next route inventory and parses modules with
the root's pinned Babel parser. It excludes declaration files and tests, records
source hashes, and never evaluates app code. The JSON includes every page,
layout, route handler with its exported methods, server-action declaration,
direct framework import, and workspace import. Imported action implementations
and transitive framework imports require a separate caller review.

The initial inventory has these counts. Regenerate it when source changes:

| App | Pages | Layouts | Local API handlers | Action modules | Direct framework imports |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Finance | 18 | 3 | 82 | 1 | 132 |
| Pay | 6 | 1 | 26 | 1 | 79 |

## Preserve Finance route ownership

Finance has 17 workspace pages plus the token verification page. Workspace
pages cover the overview, analytics, budgets, categories, debts and debt detail,
invoices and invoice creation/detail, promotions, recurring transactions, tags,
transactions and transaction detail/categories, and wallets and wallet detail.

The 82 local handlers include both `/api/workspaces/*` and
`/api/v1/workspaces/*`. Preserve every exported method and unsupported-method
response. The Next configuration sends selected workspace routes to Web before
local route matching and forwards unmatched `/api/*` requests to Web afterwards.
Port that precedence with the bridge's guarded forwarding contract. A page
catch-all must never capture an API request.

Keep the existing authorization and mutation behavior for invoices, wallet
checkpoints and reconciliation, interest, budgets, promotions, inventory, and
offline mutation replay. These handlers are not permission to change schemas,
replay an uncertain write, or move a local handler to Web.

`fetchWorkspaces` is Finance's app-owned server action. It calls
`fetchSatelliteWorkspaces` in the shared satellite package, which reads request
headers and forwards internal API authorization. Convert the complete call path
with the bridge server-function transport. Preserve same-origin CSRF protection,
session admission, and workspace visibility.

The root layout needs replacements for `next/root-params`, the Next Nuqs
adapter, shared font/metadata helpers, and Vercel analytics. Retain the current
offline provider's `register={false}` behavior. The workspace layout reads
request cookies and headers, checks membership and permissions, and renders
async shared components. Verify those components through the bridge page adapter
before expanding their children.

The proxy currently pins Vercel's `__vdpl` cookie with `Path=/`. The native
candidate must leave deployment pinning to the Vercel control path. Do not turn
that cookie into cohort identity or copy it onto the shared origin.

## Qualify both Finance URL modes

The candidate must work on both `finance.<host>` and `<host>/finance`.
The bridge owns base-path normalization and cookie serialization. Preserve the
external prefix on redirects, ordinary links, assets, action requests, and API
calls while matching the internal route once.

Use `tuturuuu_app_session_finance` and the corresponding app-specific refresh
cookie. Cookies use `Path=/finance` under the prefix and `Path=/` on the
subdomain. The shared bridge owns the 14-day legacy-cookie read window on
subdomains. Do not accept the legacy cookie on the shared origin. Cookie paths
prevent name collisions but do not establish an authorization boundary.

Acceptance covers English and Vietnamese URLs, anonymous login, cross-app token
verification, refresh and logout, MFA recovery, personal/internal workspace
aliases, invitations, permission denial, and query preservation. Inspect every
`Set-Cookie` separately. Exercise parallel requests with different users and
workspaces to detect request-context leakage.

Keep the staging profile noindex and require its exact account, Worker, origin,
bindings, and rollback mapping before publication. Source configuration alone
does not prove that a hosted staging environment exists. Follow the
[Apps artifact and runtime contract](/build/devops/apps-viteplus-cloudflare)
for sealed original/restored artifact and browser acceptance.

## Consume the shared canary decision

The canary operator owns the ladder `staff -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%`. The build
consumes the shared bridge's sticky cohort decision. Tag server observations
and client error/TTFB measurements with the same cohort and source identity.
The decision must come from the Worker; a caller-supplied cohort header must
not select staff admission or override the configured percentage. Do not expose
session tokens, user identities, or payment data in telemetry.

Each step requires at least 200 sessions **and** at least four hours, with every
gate green against the Vercel control. The operator automatically returns to
0% if any threshold is breached:

| Gate | Breach |
| --- | --- |
| 5xx rate | Greater than control plus 0.5 percentage points |
| Authentication | Any rise in loops or failures |
| p95 TTFB | Greater than 1.3 times control |
| Client errors | Greater than 1.5 times control |

Thin traffic cannot qualify a step. A stage stays pending until both duration
and session evidence are sufficient. The build must support the bridge's 0%
rollback without creating a second cohort selector or router Worker. No canary
traffic is admitted by this preparation.

## Require Pay sandbox acceptance

Pay's six pages cover the locale root, dashboard, login, token verification,
workspace billing, and billing success. Its billing action module exports six
functions for billing details, payment methods, billing address, and the
customer portal. Preserve each action's current actor and permission checks.

The 26 handlers include payment webhooks, checkout, subscription changes,
seat changes, billing invoices, credits, auth, existing cron endpoints, and
subscription migration endpoints. Inventory is not authority to invoke those
jobs or migrations. Preserve Web fallback and local payment-route precedence.

Before staging sign-off, run payment-provider sandbox acceptance for checkout
completion/cancellation, signed webhook rejection and replay, subscription and
seat changes, billing details, customer portal, and invoice delivery. Reuse the
original operation identity when a write outcome is unknown. Do not send live
payments or enable live provider bindings to obtain acceptance.

## Close the migration gates

Run exact-head unit, type, and lint checks on Sonha and the real `vp build`,
sealed-artifact verification, emitted-runtime tests, and browser acceptance on
Thanh through `ttr resources run`. Install frozen dependencies. Keep the M4 for
editing and focused source checks; it runs no builds, Docker, or local Supabase.
If its `check:changed` gate refuses admission, run the same committed source
through a Thanh bundle. Never bypass the gate.

An independent Claude review is required before integration. Keep Finance and
Pay publication held in `tuturuuu.ci.ts` and the shared publication-policy
enforcement until an explicit cutover PR admits them. Preparation cannot stand
in for the real Start build, provider sandbox, hosted acceptance, or cutover.
